overview.lead: Mages are cloth-wearing ranged casters, and all three specs (Arcane, Fire and Frost) deal damage. Blizzard sums up the class as unique buffs, conjured food and water, strong control such as Polymorph and strong single-target and area damage. The weak spot is melee range, so keep your distance.

points.text: Alliance Mages can be Human, Gnome or High Order Skyborne. Human Ruthless gives +1% crit, Gnome Eureka! makes non-periodic abilities cheaper and stronger, and Skyborne Wind-Blessed gives +2% haste.
Each tree has new talents in Forever: Arcane gains Arcane Blast and Arcane Wrath, Fire gains Heating Up, and Frost gains Ice Lance and Fingers of Frost.
First raid unlock date: 9 December 2026, for The Barrow Deeps, Hyjal Summit and Onyxia's Lair.

101.summary: What every Mage should know before choosing a spec: what Forever changed, the class quests and the racial choice.

steps.text: Train every new rank of your main spells: spells cast far below your level get less from spell power and are less likely to trigger talents.
From level 40 the trainer teaches Frostfire Bolt, a 3 sec cast that counts as Fire and Frost, uses your higher Fire or Frost spell damage and hits the target's lower resistance.
Apply your own debuffs: Improved Scorch, Winter's Chill and Ignite now help only the Mage who applies them.
Get spell hit from Precision in the Frost tree, which now gives 2%, 4% or 6% with all spells. Arcane Focus is gone.
Ice Block is now the 16-point Frost talent and Cold Snap the 21-point one, with a 10 min cooldown.

mistakes.mistake: Down-ranking Frostbolt to save mana, as in Classic.
mistakes.fix: Spells cast far below your level lose spell power and talent procs. Blizzard's example is a rank 1 Frostbolt at 60, which has no Frostbite chance.

mistakes.mistake: Waiting for another Mage's Scorch stacks.
mistakes.fix: Improved Scorch now helps only the Mage who applies it, so apply your own.

mistakes.mistake: Looking for Arcane Focus to get spell hit.
mistakes.fix: Blizzard removed it. Precision in Frost gives 2%, 4% or 6% hit with all spells.

steps.text: Warcraft Tavern's beta leveling guide lists Mage class quests at levels 10, 15 and 26, with rewards such as robes, staves, off-hands and wands.
Visit a portal trainer at 20 for Teleport: Stormwind and Teleport: Ironforge, and at 30 for Teleport: Darnassus. Warcraft Tavern lists Rune of Teleportation as the reagent.
Portals follow at 40 (Stormwind and Ironforge) and 50 (Darnassus), with Rune of Portals as the reagent.
Use Comprehend Scroll, in the General tab of your spellbook, to decipher scrolls that creatures drop. Blizzard leaves the rewards for players to find.
Conjure Water makes 20 bottles per cast, and Conjure Food rank 6 makes 20 sweet rolls.

mistakes.mistake: Looking for Teleport: Dalaran at the class trainer.
mistakes.fix: The trainer does not sell it, and how you get it is unconfirmed: treat it as a datamine hint.

mistakes.mistake: Deciphering scrolls in a dangerous spot.
mistakes.fix: Beta reports say a failed decipher turns you into a sheep until the skill improves.

steps.text: A Human Mage gets +1% crit from Ruthless, cut from 2% on 26 October, and +10% Spirit.
A Gnome Mage gets Eureka!, an 8 sec buff that makes non-periodic abilities 10% cheaper and stronger.
A High Order Skyborne Mage gets +2% haste from Wind-Blessed. Its Attuned bonus is removed when you enter a raid.

mistakes.fix: Attuned is removed when you enter a raid.

mistakes.mistake: Using an older guide that gives Ruthless 2% crit.
mistakes.fix: Ruthless is +1% crit since the 26 October notes.

overview.lead: Arcane is built on two new talents. Arcane Blast stacks a buff that turns part of your Intellect into spell damage, while making Arcane Blast itself more expensive. Arcane Wrath is a slow, heavy nuke on a short cooldown that scales with your maximum mana.

points.text: Your burst comes from Presence of Mind (your next Mage spell with a cast time under 10 sec becomes instant) and Arcane Power (15 sec of 30% more damage at 30% more mana cost). Arcane Power requires Presence of Mind.
Intellect matters a lot here: Arcane Blast converts it into spell damage, Arcane Wrath scales with your maximum mana and Arcane Mind raises your Intellect.

101.summary: Leveling as Arcane, the Arcane Blast rotation and the habits that matter first.

steps.text: Arcane Blast sits on row 3 of the Arcane tree and Arcane Wrath on row 4, and Arcane Wrath requires Arcane Blast.
At rank 1, Missile Barrage (row 2) gives Arcane Blast a 20% chance, and Arcane Wrath, Fireball, Frostbolt and Frostfire Bolt a 10% chance, to make your next Arcane Missiles free and faster.
Warcraft Tavern says Frost has mostly been used for leveling, so pick Arcane because you like how it plays.
Conjure your own water (20 bottles per cast) and food to cut downtime between pulls.
Train every new rank: spells cast far below your level get less from spell power and trigger talents less often.

mistakes.mistake: Skipping Arcane Blast on the way to Arcane Wrath.
mistakes.fix: Arcane Wrath requires Arcane Blast.

mistakes.mistake: Waiting for Arcane Missiles itself to trigger Missile Barrage.
mistakes.fix: Its rank text names Arcane Blast, Arcane Wrath, Fireball, Frostbolt and Frostfire Bolt as the spells that trigger it.

steps.text: Build Arcane Blast stacks first, up to 4. Each cast adds 12% of your Intellect as spell damage and raises the next Arcane Blast's mana cost by 100%.
Cast Arcane Wrath whenever its 6 sec cooldown is ready. It is a 3.5 sec cast that gains spell damage equal to 5% of your maximum mana.
Spend Missile Barrage procs on Arcane Missiles: a proc halves the channel, makes it free and fires a missile every 0.5 sec.
Press Presence of Mind and Arcane Power together when the group needs burst: Arcane Power gives 15 sec of 30% more damage at 30% more mana cost.
When mana runs low, let your Arcane Blast stacks fall off. They last 18 sec from the first cast.

mistakes.mistake: Chaining Arcane Blast until your mana is gone.
mistakes.fix: Each stack raises Arcane Blast's mana cost by 100%. Let the stacks expire after 18 sec and recover.

mistakes.mistake: Holding Arcane Wrath for a big moment.
mistakes.fix: It has a 6 sec cooldown, so cast it whenever it is ready.

steps.text: Arcane Subtlety lowers the threat of your Arcane spells by 15% and the target's resistance to all your spells by 8 at rank 1.
One point in Improved Counterspell adds a 2 sec silence to Counterspell, and the second makes it 4 sec.
Arcane Geometry adds 3 yards of range to your Arcane spells, or 6 yards with both points.
Improved Channeling at 5/5 keeps Arcane Missiles from losing time to damage and gives Arcane Blast and Arcane Wrath a 70% chance of the same.

mistakes.mistake: Expecting Counterspell to silence without the talent.
mistakes.fix: The silence comes from Improved Counterspell: 2 sec at rank 1.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling threat with Arcane spells on a boss.
mistakes.fix: Arcane Subtlety cuts the threat of your Arcane spells by 15% at rank 1 and 30% at rank 2.

overview.lead: Fire turns critical strikes into more damage. Crits from Fireball, Frostfire Bolt, Fire Blast and Scorch build Heating Up, which shortens your next Pyroblast, and Fire crits also feed your Ignite.

points.text: Combustion is your burst button: each Fire hit adds 10% Fire crit chance until you land 3 non-periodic Fire crits.
Improved Scorch and Ignite are personal in Forever, so every Fire Mage keeps their own going.

101.summary: Leveling as Fire, the Heating Up rotation and the habits that matter first.

steps.text: Pyroblast is a row-3 talent, and Heating Up, on row 4, requires it.
Impact gives your Fire spells a 3% chance at rank 1 to stun the target for 2 sec.
Blast Wave damages every enemy around you and dazes them to 50% movement speed for 6 sec. It has a 45 sec cooldown.
Burning Soul gives your Fire spells a 23% chance not to lose casting time when you take damage and cuts their threat by 10% at rank 1.
Keep your main spells at their top rank: spells cast far below your level trigger talents less often.

mistakes.mistake: Leveling with a low-rank Fireball to save mana.

steps.text: Keep your own Improved Scorch debuff stacked: each stack raises your Fire damage against the target by 3%, up to 5 stacks for 30 sec. Scorch applies it 33% of the time at rank 1 and every time at 3/3.
Fireball is your main cast. From level 40, Frostfire Bolt is an option if your build also takes Frost talents.
Press Fire Blast on cooldown: every Fire Blast that deals damage adds a Heating Up stack.
At 3 Heating Up stacks, cast Pyroblast: it drops to a 1.5 sec cast. The buff lasts 20 sec.
Use Combustion for burst, ideally while Improved Scorch is fully stacked.

mistakes.mistake: Letting Heating Up run out.

mistakes.mistake: Waiting for another Mage's Scorch stacks.

steps.text: The Fire tree holds 46 points, so a full Fire build always spends some points in another tree.
Master of Elements refunds 10% of the base mana cost of your Fire and Frost crits at rank 1.
Incineration also raises the crit chance of Ice Lance and Arcane Blast, which helps hybrid builds.
Improved Fire Blast cuts Fire Blast's cooldown by 1 sec and adds 8 yards of range at rank 1, which means more Heating Up stacks over a fight.

mistakes.fix: It refunds only your Fire and Frost critical strikes.

overview.lead: Frost controls the fight. Your Chill effects slow enemies, Frostbite can freeze them, Fingers of Frost makes your next spells treat them as Frozen, and Shatter and Ice Lance punish Frozen targets.

points.text: Warcraft Tavern says Frost has mostly been used for leveling and PvP.
In raids Frost no longer gives a shared debuff: Winter's Chill now only powers your own Cone of Cold.

101.summary: Leveling as Frost, the Frozen-target rotation and the habits that matter first.

steps.text: Ice Lance sits on row 3, Ice Block on row 4 and Cold Snap on row 5, and Ice Barrier on row 7 requires Cold Snap.
Frost farms less well than in Classic: Cone of Cold slows for less time, and Improved Blizzard's slow tops out at 40% at 3/3.
Frost Blast was removed. Slow with Frostbolt, make space with Frost Nova, and use Cone of Cold when the pack closes in.
Frost Warding raises the armor and resistances from Frost Armor and Ice Armor by 15% at rank 1.

mistakes.mistake: Planning Classic-style mass kiting with Cone of Cold and Blizzard.
mistakes.fix: Cone of Cold slows for less time and Improved Blizzard's slow is capped lower in Forever.

mistakes.mistake: Skipping Cold Snap on the way to Ice Barrier.
mistakes.fix: Ice Barrier requires Cold Snap.

steps.text: Frostbolt is your main spell, and it is the spell that applies Winter's Chill.
When Fingers of Frost procs, your next spell treats the target as Frozen. Follow with Ice Lance, which deals 300% more damage to Frozen targets.
Build Winter's Chill stacks, up to 5, before Cone of Cold: each stack makes that Cone of Cold hit harder.
Improved Frost Nova shortens Frost Nova's cooldown by 2 sec at rank 1, so you can freeze targets for Shatter more often.
Ice Barrier absorbs damage and stops pushback while it holds, and Ice Block makes you immune for 10 sec.

mistakes.mistake: Casting Ice Lance on a target that is not Frozen.
mistakes.fix: Its bonus damage applies to Frozen targets, and Fingers of Frost lets your next spell treat the target as Frozen. Without either, cast Frostbolt.

steps.text: Shatter no longer needs Improved Frost Nova, and it adds 17% crit against Frozen targets at rank 1.
Cold Snap has a 10 min cooldown and finishes the remaining cooldown on all your other Frost spells.
Frostfire Bolt, a trainer spell from level 40, uses your higher Fire or Frost spell damage against the target's lower resistance.
Permafrost makes your Chill effects last 11% longer and slow by another 3% at rank 1.

mistakes.mistake: Using Cold Snap at the start of a pull and having nothing left for an emergency.
mistakes.fix: It has a 10 min cooldown. Keep it to bring back Ice Block or Frost Nova when you need them.

steps.text: Open a build in the talent calculator and check it against your talents in game before you spend points.

Winter's Chill at 5/5 applies on every Frostbolt and every Ice Lance that Fingers of Frost empowers.
The Frost tree holds 48 points, and Precision gives 6% hit with all spells at 3/3.

Ice Lance and Fire Blast share an 8-second cooldown, and Frozen targets take Ice Lance's 300% damage bonus.
Frostfire Bolt counts as Fire and Frost: Blizzard's example has Ignite plus Ice Shards making its crits deal 280%.

Ice Block gives 10 sec of immunity, but you cannot act while it lasts.
Every raider carries their own Drakefire Amulet into Onyxia's Lair, and Blizzard asks for fire resistance before the fight.

steps.text: Frost Nova into Shatter is your burst: a Frozen target takes Ice Lance's 300% bonus damage plus Shatter's extra crit chance.

Ice Block gives 10 sec of immunity on a 5 min cooldown, and Cold Snap finishes its cooldown.
